newsitem.title: USA: Chicago's Sears Tower claws back "tallest" title.
newsitem.headline: Chicago's Sears Tower claws back "tallest" title.

text.p: The title of world's tallest building held by Kuala Lumpur's Petronas Towers was divvied up on Thursday to include two dethroned champions in the United States, the group arbitrating such matters declared.

The Pennsylvania-based Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat decided the 110-floor black glass-and-steel Sears Tower in Chicago holds the records for highest occupied floor at 1,431 feet (436 metres) and highest rooftop (1,450 feet) (442 metres).

The architectural and engineering group held a ceremony on the Sears Tower rooftop to lay a plaque and massage egos damaged in April, 1996, when Malaysia's twin Petronas Towers took the title of world's tallest building.

But the group's new chairman, architect R. Shankar Nair, noted that in its first category of bigness, the 88-floor Petronas Towers retained the title as the tallest skyscraper including a structural or architectural top with a height of 1,483 feet (452 m) because of the towers' 242-foot (74 metre)-tall unoccupied steel spires.

The overall champion may still be New York's World Trade Centre. In the council's fourth and final category, which included previously ignored television antennae, the twin Manhattan monoliths topped out at 1,728 feet (527 metres).

The World Trade Centre held the world's tallest building title when it was finished in 1972 but was eclipsed a year later by the Sears Tower. A planned Shanghai skyscraper, at 1,509 feet (460 metres), will leave them all in its shadow.
